documents.title: Booking Policies & Procedures
documents.summary: Standard operating procedures for handling travel bookings across all channels
documents.body:
# Booking Policies & Procedures

## Overview

This document outlines the standard operating procedures for handling travel bookings across all channels — online, phone, email, and in-person. All staff must follow these procedures to ensure consistent, compliant service.

## Booking Channels

### Online Bookings
- **Self-service portal**: Customers can book directly via the website. All online bookings are confirmed immediately and followed by an automated confirmation email.
- **API/OTA integrations**: Third-party bookings (Expedia, Booking.com, etc.) flow through automated API connections. Monitor the integration dashboard daily for sync errors.

### Phone Bookings
- Agents must verify caller identity before making any changes to existing bookings.
- Read back all booking details before finalizing: dates, destinations, passenger names, and total cost.
- Record consent for call monitoring and data processing per GDPR/privacy regulations.

### Email Bookings
- Respond within 4 business hours for standard inquiries.
- Include a booking reference number in every confirmation reply.
- Never process payment details received via unencrypted email.

## Booking Lifecycle

1. **Search & Select**: Customer selects travel products (flights, hotels, packages)
2. **Quote**: Provide a binding or non-binding quote depending on fare type
3. **Booking Hold**: Non-refundable deposit holds the booking for 24–48 hours
4. **Payment Collection**: Full payment required before ticketing/release
5. **Confirmation**: Send comprehensive itinerary with booking references
6. **Pre-travel**: Send reminders at 7 days, 48 hours, and 24 hours before departure
7. **Post-travel**: Follow up for feedback and review within 48 hours of return

## Payment Terms

| Payment Type | Timing | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Full payment | At booking | Required for non-refundable/non-changeable fares |
| Deposit + balance | Deposit due at quote, balance 30 days before travel | For packages and group bookings |
| Installment plan | Available for bookings >$2,000 | 3 equal payments, final due 45 days before travel |

## Cancellation Policy

- **Standard fares**: Full refund minus cancellation fee ($50–$200 depending on product)
- **Non-refundable fares**: No refund, but may offer travel credit minus fee
- **Group bookings (10+ passengers)**: Special cancellation terms apply per contract
- **Force majeure**: Waive fees for government-mandated travel restrictions, natural disasters

## Refund Processing

- Process within 7 business days of approved cancellation
- Refunds to original payment method whenever possible
- Travel credits issued when refund to original payment is not possible
- Escalate refund exceptions to the refunds team via the refund request form

documents.title: Fare Rules & Pricing Guidelines
documents.summary: Comprehensive fare rules and pricing guidelines for air, hotel, and package bookings
documents.body:
# Fare Rules & Pricing Guidelines

## Overview

This document defines fare rules and pricing guidelines applicable to all travel products sold. Pricing accuracy is critical — errors can result in financial loss and regulatory penalties.

## Fare Types

### Air Fares
| Fare Class | Changeable | Refundable | Baggage Allowance |
|---|---|---|---|
| Economy Light | No | No | Carry-on only |
| Economy Standard | Yes ($50 fee) | No | 1 checked bag |
| Economy Flex | Yes (no fee) | Yes (minus $75) | 2 checked bags |
| Business | Yes (no fee) | Yes (full refund) | 2 checked bags + priority |
| First Class | Yes (no fee) | Yes (full refund) | 3 checked bags + full service |

### Hotel Rate Types
- **BAR (Best Available Rate)**: Dynamic pricing, changes daily based on demand
- **Package Rate**: Bundled pricing with flights/transfers — typically 10–20% below BAR
- **Corporate Rate**: Pre-negotiated discount for partner companies
- **Group Rate**: Block booking pricing for 10+ rooms
- **Promotional Rate**: Time-limited discounts (advance purchase, last minute, seasonal)

### Package Pricing
- Packages combine flight + hotel + transfers at a bundled discount
- Minimum 15% savings vs booking components separately
- Dynamic package pricing recalculated every 15 minutes

## Pricing Rules

### Currency & Rounding
- All prices displayed in local currency of the departure country
- Round to the nearest whole currency unit
- Display price breakdown (flight, hotel, taxes, fees, service charge) on quote

### Taxes & Fees
| Item | Rate | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Sales Tax/VAT | Varies by jurisdiction | Applied to service fees, not to third-party product costs |
| Service Fee | 5–12% of total | Disclosed before booking confirmation |
| Airport Tax | Included in fare | Never shown as separate line item |
| Tourism Tax | Varies by destination | Collected at point of stay (hotel) |
| Carbon Offset | Optional, $5–$20 | Customer opt-in at checkout |

### Price Guarantees
- **Price Match**: If customer finds a lower published rate for the identical product, we match it and give 10% of the difference as credit
- **Price Drop Protection**: If the price drops after booking, customer receives the difference as travel credit (must claim within 24 hours of booking)

## Fare Filing & Updates

- Fares are updated nightly from GDS and supplier feeds
- Manual overrides require manager approval
- Bulk fare updates must be tested in staging environment before production deployment

## Error Handling

| Error Type | Response | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Pricing display error | Fix within 2 hours | Pricing team |
| Incorrect fare filed | Correct within 24 hours | Content team |
| Currency conversion error | Fix and audit all affected bookings | Finance team |
| Discount applied incorrectly | Re-process with correct pricing | Billing team |

documents.title: Destination Guides — Standards & Template
documents.summary: Standard template and quality guidelines for creating destination guide content
documents.body:
# Destination Guides — Standards & Template

## Overview

Destination guides are a key differentiator for our travel services. Every guide must follow this template to ensure consistent quality, SEO performance, and customer satisfaction.

## Required Sections

Every destination guide MUST include these sections:

### 1. Overview
- Quick-reference stats: country, capital, language, currency, timezone, plug type
- 2–3 sentence introduction to the destination
- Best time to visit (by season and activity type)

### 2. Getting There
- Major airports and airline routes
- Visa requirements by nationality (with links to official sources)
- Airport transfer options (train, bus, taxi, rideshare) with approximate costs

### 3. Getting Around
- Public transportation options
- Car rental requirements (license, age, insurance)
- Ride-hailing availability
- Safety tips for travelers

### 4. Accommodation
- Recommended areas/neighborhoods to stay
- Hotel price ranges (budget, mid-range, luxury)
- Unique accommodation options (boutique, resort, homestay)

### 5. Things to Do
- Top 10 attractions (with approximate visit duration and ticket prices)
- Free/inexpensive activities
- Day trips from the city
- Seasonal events and festivals

### 6. Food & Drink
- Local specialties and must-try dishes
- Restaurant recommendations (budget, mid-range, fine dining)
- Dietary restriction guidance
- Street food safety tips

### 7. Safety & Health
- Emergency numbers (police, ambulance, fire)
- Recommended vaccinations
- Travel insurance recommendations
- Common scams to watch for
- LGBTQ+ travel considerations

### 8. Practical Information
- Tipping customs
- Business hours (shops, banks, restaurants)
- Connectivity (SIM cards, WiFi availability)
- Electrical adapters needed

## Quality Standards

| Standard | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Word count | 1,500–3,000 words per guide |
| Accuracy | Every factual claim verified within 30 days of publish |
| Freshness | Full review every 6 months; update when major changes occur |
| Images | Minimum 5 original or properly licensed images |
| Internal links | Link to related destinations, packages, and policies |
| External links | Link to official tourism board and embassy/consulate sites |
| SEO | Primary keyword in title, H1, first paragraph, and meta description |
| Accessibility | Alt text on all images; readable font size; color contrast compliant |

## Review Process

1. Draft written by content team
2. Fact-check by research team
3. SEO review by marketing team
4. Legal review for destinations with active travel advisories
5. Final approval by content manager before publication

documents.title: Travel Regulations & Compliance
documents.summary: Key travel regulations, consumer rights, and compliance requirements across jurisdictions
documents.body:
# Travel Regulations & Compliance

## Overview

This document covers the key regulations, consumer rights, and compliance requirements applicable to travel services. Non-compliance can result in fines, license revocation, and legal liability.

## Regulatory Framework

### Key Legislation by Region

| Region | Key Regulation | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| United States | DOT Regulations (14 CFR Part 374a) | Air travel consumer protection |
| European Union | Package Travel Directive (EU 2015/2302) | Package holidays and linked travel arrangements |
| United Kingdom | Package Travel and Linked Travel Arrangements Regulations 2018 | Post-Brexit equivalent of EU directive |
| Australia | Australian Consumer Law (ACL) + Travel Compensation Fund | Consumer guarantees and fund membership |
| Canada | Air Passenger Protection Regulations (APPR) | Air passenger rights |
| UAE | Federal Law No. 8 of 1984 (Commercial Transactions) | Agency and commercial travel regulation |

## Consumer Rights

### Right to Information
Customers must receive, before booking:
- Full price breakdown (product cost, taxes, fees, charges)
- Terms and conditions of the fare/package
- Cancellation and refund policy
- Passport and visa requirements
- Health formalities and safety information

### Right to Cancel
- **14-day cooling-off period** for online/distance bookings (EU/UK)
- Right to cancel before departure with reasonable notice
- **Force majeure cancellation**: Full refund (not credit) when government travel restrictions apply

### Right to Refund
- Full refund within 14 days of cancellation acceptance
- Alternative equivalent booking offered at no extra cost when available

## Data Protection & Privacy

### GDPR Compliance (EU/UK customers)
- Obtain explicit consent for data processing
- Retain customer data only as long as necessary for the booking
- Right to data access, rectification, and erasure
- Data breach notification within 72 hours

### PCI-DSS Compliance (Payment Data)
- Never store full credit card numbers, CVV codes, or magnetic stripe data
- Use PCI-compliant payment processor
- Tokenize payment references for recurring billing

## Licensing Requirements

| Jurisdiction | License Required | Renewal |
|---|---|---|
| USA (most states) | Seller of Travel license | Annual |
| EU | No centralized license; registration with local tourism authority | Varies |
| UK | ATOL (Air Travel Organiser’s Licence) for flight-inclusive packages | Annual |
| Australia | Travel Compensation Fund membership | Annual |
| Canada | TICO (Ontario) / OPC (Quebec) / provincial registration | Annual |

## Reporting Obligations

### Regular Reports
- Monthly sales data to tourism authorities (where required)
- Quarterly financial reports to licensing bodies
- Annual compliance audit

### Incident Reporting
Report to regulatory authority within:
- 24 hours: Serious safety incident
- 72 hours: Customer complaint involving regulatory breach
- 7 days: Data breach (unless higher severity)

## Enforcement & Penalties

| Violation | Maximum Penalty |
|---|---|
| Operating without required license | $10,000–$50,000 per incident |
| Misleading pricing | Up to $100,000 (EU) |
| Failure to protect customer funds | License revocation + fine |
| Data breach (negligence) | Up to 4% of global revenue (GDPR) |

documents.title: Customer Service Standards — Travel
documents.summary: Service standards and protocols for delivering exceptional travel customer support
documents.body:
# Customer Service Standards — Travel

## Overview

These standards define the level of service every customer can expect when interacting with our travel support team. First-response quality and speed directly impact customer retention and brand reputation.

## Service Level Targets

| Channel | First Response | Resolution Time | Hours |
|---|---|---|---|
| Phone | Immediate | < 15 min | 24/7 |
| Email | < 4 hours | < 24 hours | 24/7 |
| Live Chat | < 2 min | < 10 min | 24/7 |
| Social Media DM | < 1 hour | < 8 hours | 06:00–22:00 local |
| SMS/WhatsApp | < 5 min | < 15 min | 24/7 |

## Communication Tone & Style

- **Empathetic & calm**: Travel is stressful when things go wrong. Always acknowledge the customer’s feelings first.
- **Solution-focused**: Lead with what you CAN do, not what you cannot.
- **Clear & concise**: Avoid jargon. Confirm understanding by asking the customer to repeat back critical details.
- **Proactive**: If you see a potential issue (delays, weather, overbooking), reach out before the customer does.

## Common Travel Scenarios

### Flight Delay or Cancellation
1. **Acknowledge**: "I’m sorry for the disruption to your travel plans."
2. **Inform**: Check the reason (airline-caused vs. weather/force majeure)
3. **Options**:
   - Rebook on next available flight (same airline or partner)
   - Offer meal/voucher if delay > 2 hours (airline-caused)
   - Offer hotel + transport if overnight delay (airline-caused)
   - Full refund if cancellation and no suitable alternative
4. **Follow up**: Send updated itinerary and confirm contact info

### Lost or Delayed Baggage
1. **Log claim**: Create baggage irregularity report (PIR) in the airline’s system
2. **Provide essentials**: Reimbursement for essentials (up to airline policy limit)
3. **Track**: Provide PIR reference and tracking link
4. **Deliver**: Arrange delivery to customer’s accommodation when found
5. **Compensation**: Process compensation claim per airline policy (usually after 21 days)

### Travel Disruption (Weather/Natural Disaster)
1. **Safety first**: Confirm customer safety before discussing logistics
2. **Information**: Provide official updates from local authorities
3. **Accommodation**: Arrange emergency accommodation if stranded
4. **Repatriation**: Coordinate with embassy/consulate if needed
5. **Documentation**: Document all communications for insurance claims

### Booking Issue (Wrong Name, Date, Destination)
1. **Assess**: Is the error ours or the customer’s?
2. **Our error**: Fix at no cost, offer goodwill credit
3. **Customer error**: Explain available options and fees
4. **Name correction**: Most airlines allow within 24 hours or for a fee
5. **Date change**: Refer to fare rules for change fees and fare differences

## Escalation Matrix

| Issue Type | L1 Support | L2 Support (Team Lead) | L3 (Manager) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Simple booking change | ✅ | — | — |
| Flight rebooking (delay) | ✅ | — | — |
| Refund request | ✅ | — | — |
| Customer complaint | — | ✅ | — |
| Compensation > $500 | — | ✅ | — |
| Legal/regulatory issue | — | — | ✅ |
| VIP/Executive customer | — | — | ✅ |
| PR-sensitive situation | — | — | ✅ |

## Quality Assurance

- Random sampling: 5% of interactions audited weekly
- Target: CSAT > 85%, First Contact Resolution > 70%
- Calibration sessions: Bi-weekly with the whole support team

documents.title: Travel Supplier Management
documents.summary: Guidelines for managing relationships with travel suppliers: airlines, hotels, DMCs, and tour operators
documents.body:
# Travel Supplier Management

## Overview

Effective supplier relationships are the foundation of a successful travel business. This document covers supplier onboarding, management, performance monitoring, and offboarding procedures.

## Supplier Categories

1. **Airlines** — Scheduled and charter carriers
2. **Accommodation** — Hotels, resorts, vacation rentals, hostels
3. **Ground Transport** — Transfers, car rentals, rail, coach
4. **Tour Operators / DMCs** — In-destination services, excursions, guided tours
5. **Insurance Providers** — Travel insurance, cancellation protection
6. **Technology Partners** — GDS providers, booking engines, CRM systems

## Supplier Onboarding

### Due Diligence Requirements
| Requirement | Description |
|---|---|
| Business registration | Valid business license in country of operation |
| Insurance | Professional liability + public liability insurance (minimum $2M) |
| Compliance | Adherence to local consumer protection laws |
| Financial health | Recent financial statements or credit check |
| References | Minimum 2 client references |
| Safety audit | For transport and activity suppliers — safety certification |

### Contract Essentials
- Service description and standards
- Pricing and commission structure
- Payment terms (NET 30 standard)
- Cancellation and change policies
- Liability and indemnification clauses
- Data processing agreement (GDPR compliance)
- Force majeure provisions
- Termination terms (min 30 days notice)
- Dispute resolution (arbitration recommended)

## Performance Monitoring

### Key Performance Indicators
| KPI | Target | Measurement |
|---|---|---|
| Booking fulfillment rate | > 98% | Successful bookings / total requests |
| Response time (urgent) | < 2 hours | Time to acknowledge urgent query |
| Customer satisfaction | > 85% | Post-trip survey scores |
| Price accuracy | > 99.5% | Correct prices / total quotes |
| Complaint rate | < 2% | Complaints / total bookings |

### Review Cadence
- **Monthly**: Operational review (performance metrics, issue tracking)
- **Quarterly**: Strategic review (market trends, joint business planning)
- **Annual**: Full contract review and renewal negotiation

## Issue Resolution

### Dispute Process
1. **L1**: Day-to-day issues resolved by account manager and supplier contact
2. **L2**: Formal written dispute if unresolved after 5 business days
3. **L3**: Escalation to management — mediation or arbitration

### Common Issues & Remedies
| Issue | First Step | Escalation |
|---|---|---|
| Overbooking | Request alternate equivalent accommodation | L2 after 2 hours |
| Price discrepancy | Match quoted price or cancel without penalty | L2 after 24 hours |
| Quality complaint | Collect evidence, request remediation | L3 if unresolved |
| Payment dispute | Review contract terms, request payment proof | L3 |

## Supplier Offboarding

- 30-day notice (or per contract terms)
- Settle all outstanding invoices
- Migrate data and active bookings
- Conduct exit interview
- Document reason for offboarding
- Archive all contracts and correspondence

## Preferred Supplier Program

Qualified suppliers receive:
- Priority placement in search results and packages
- Reduced commission rate (in exchange for volume commitment)
- Marketing support (featured content, social media, email)
- Early access to new product launches
